ellie (support): escalating: ACME reported that our function-calling fanout returned mismatched tool_results — invoice JSONs were applied to the wrong customer id and billing shows token charges double. Customer hit prod around 11:02 UTC, high severity. attaching example payload + logs below.
ellie (support): repro steps in prod: 1) user calls /v1/chat.completions with functions=[lookup_customer, render_invoice] and mode=parallel 2) we fan out both calls to internal tool runners 3) response merged but customer_id in final payload belonged to tool A while invoice from tool B.

```json
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-2",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Please generate invoice for customer 4234 for March"}],
  "function_calls": ["lookup_customer","render_invoice"],
  "parallel_tool_invocation": true
}
```

ellie (support): returned merged response (snip):

```json
{
  "tool_results": [
    {"tool":"lookup_customer","result": {"id":4234, "name":"Acme"}},
    {"tool":"render_invoice","result": {"invoice_id":"inv_998","customer_id":8122}}
  ],
  "merged_output": {"invoice_id":"inv_998","customer_id":4234}
}
```

thomas (oncall): reducer is matching by arrival order but downstream merge expects original function order. seems like we lost the original invocation index.
jake (eng-runtime): that matches a hypothesis I had earlier — the fanout table uses unordered set and reducer iterates arrival order. quick patch: tag each invocation with invocation_index and persist to reduce key so we can re-order deterministically. will run a canary.
sri (eng-ml): also saw malformed args occasionally when tools are invoked with proto v1 vs v2 schema. if the schema mismatch causes a retry, the retry may get a new call-id and flip ordering. check for 400->retry logic.

thomas (oncall): grep shows occasional 422 validation for render_invoice on runner-7 at 11:02:10.820 -> it retried once. call-988 was a retry (new id) but returned faster. that explains seq=1 for the retry.
